chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v01] The external means is clearly distinguished by its named arrangement.

[tal-a06-v10] That same emptiness-form of consciousness is sung; for yogis, by not-this reflection, that is the supreme state.

[tal-a06-v02] Place difference is declared threefold: in breath, in body, and outside.

[tal-a06-v03] The external supports include circle, altar, vessel, rosary, book, linga, drum, cloth, book, image, and form.

[tal-a06-v04] Thus the external is elevenfold and may become manyfold; there the breath support arrangement is taught.

[tal-a06-v05] The whole sixfold path, though extensive, is established in breath.

[tal-a06-v06] The movement of the path is established as ordered and unordered.

[tal-a06-v07] Supreme time abides in consciousness; that same supreme power of god is sung.

[tal-a06-v08] That same power, outside consciousness, makes ordered and unordered clear as breath movement.

[tal-a06-v09] Pure consciousness, light and supreme meaning, shines distinct like sky when the measured self is abandoned.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C6 atha śrītantrāloke sthānaprakalpākhyatayā sphuṭastu bāhyo@bhyupāyaḥ pravivicyate@tha sthānabhedastridhā proktaḥ prāṇe dehe bahistathā / prāṇaśca pañcadhā dehe dvidhā bāhyāntaratvataḥ maṇḍalaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pātramakṣasūtraṃ sapustakam / liṅgaṃ tūraṃ paṭaḥ pustaṃ pratimā mūrtireva ca ityekādaśadhā bāhyaṃ punastadbahudhā bhavet / tatra prāṇāśrayaṃ tāvadvidhānamupadiśyate adhvā samasta evāyaṃ ṣaḍvidho@pyativistṛtaḥ / yo vakṣyate sa ekatra prāṇe tāvatpratiṣṭhitaḥ adhvanaḥ kalanaṃ yattatkramākramatayā sthitam / kramākramau hi citraikakalanā bhāvagocare kramākramātmā kālaśca paraḥ saṃvidi vartate / kālī nāma parā śaktiḥ saiva devasya gīyate saiva saṃvidbahiḥ svātmagarbhībhūtau kramākramau / sphuṭayantī prarohaṇa prāṇavṛttiriti sthitā saṃvinmātraṃ hi yacchuddhaṃ prakāśaparamārthakam / tanmeyamātmanaḥ projjhya viviktaṃ bhāsate nabhaḥ tadeva śūnyarūpatvaṃ saṃvidaḥ parigīyate / neti neti vimarśena yogināṃ sā parā daśā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v11] That space-self, when divided and measured, becomes ready to appropriate and is named breath pulse wave.

[tal-a06-v12] Therefore they say consciousness transformed in breath, and the inner instrument principle became wind support.

[tal-a06-v13] This is that prana power, called spanda, sphuratta, jiva, and hrt-pratibha.

[tal-a06-v14] That prana activity, through five forms including prana, makes the body its own, and consciousness-full shines by that.

[tal-a06-v15] Deluded people, seeing movement born of the body pervaded by prana-activity and consciousness, think there is nothing else.

[tal-a06-v16] Materialists, calling themselves truth-seers, make authoritative that very view mostly known to children, fools, and women.

[tal-a06-v17] Their meditation becomes firm continuously; at the breaking of that body they become asleep, from destruction of the seeing-habit.

[tal-a06-v18] When that habit is destroyed, another undiminished habit of theirs, awakened, arises from somewhere and produces various abundance of fruit.

[tal-a06-v19] From lack of firmness and suspicion, from eastern habit state, and from laxity in other duty with possible latency, another habit arises.

[tal-a06-v20] From omission of duty by unfirmed other people, they call this atheistic habit, more sinful than sin.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sa eva khātmā meye@sminbhedite svīkriyonmukhaḥ / patansamucchalattvena prāṇaspandormisaṃjñitaḥ tenāhuḥ kila saṃvitprākprāṇe pariṇatā tathā / antaḥkaraṇatattvasya vāyurāśrayatāṃ gataḥ iyaṃ sā prāṇanāśaktirāntarodyogadohadā / spandaḥ sphurattā viśrāntirjīvo hṛtpratibhā matā sā prāṇavṛttiḥ prāṇādyai rūpaiḥ pañcabhirātmasāt / dehaṃ yatkurute saṃvitpūrṇastenaiṣa bhāsate prāṇanāvṛttitādātmyasaṃvitkhacitadehajām / ceṣṭāṃ paśyantyato mugdhā nāstyanyaditi manvate tāmeva bālamūrkhastrīprāyaveditṛsaṃśritām / matiṃ pramāṇīkurvantaścārvākāstattvadarśinaḥ teṣāṃ tathā bhāvanā caddārḍhyameti nirantaram / taddehabhaṅge suptāḥ syurātādṛgvāsanākṣayāt tadvāsanākṣaye tveṣāmakṣīṇaṃ vāsanāntaram / buddhaṃ kutaścitsaṃsūte vicitrāṃ phalasampadam adārḍhyaśaṅkanātprācyavāsanātādavasthyataḥ / anyakartavyaśaithilyātsaṃbhāvyānuśayatvataḥ atadrūḍhānyajanatākartavyaparilopanāt / nāstikyavāsanāmāhuḥ pāpātpāpīyasīmimām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v21] Enough of digression; now the subject is distinguished: the whole path is indeed established in prana.

[tal-a06-v22] That path is divided in two ways, by action and form; prana is indeed the crest spoken of in Srimat Trishiras.

[tal-a06-v23] Bound at sacrifice time, from formlessness it is Shiva-nature; because in day and night there are twenty-four movements.

[tal-a06-v24] Night and moon, giving various fruit through prana dispersion, and apana and sound, stand in one place.

[tal-a06-v25] The living sun does not rise halfway; in such twilight the sun faces upward, the moon faces downward, and fire is between.

[tal-a06-v26] Midday is liberation-giving: the sun stands in the middle of the sky, its essence has not set, and it awakens the wheel of creatures.

[tal-a06-v27] Point, breath, day, and sun stand together in one place; the great twilight is the third, very peaceful in nature, and established.

[tal-a06-v28] Thus where the bound crest assigns fruits, therefore in consciousness all this path stands after resting.

[tal-a06-v29] The appearance of form and action from formless, all-pervading, actionless consciousness is indeed the path of the great lord.

[tal-a06-v30] The path is to be traversed by stages; for dualists it is a cause of arrival, while for the awakened it is aimed from the enjoyable state.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-alamaprastutenātha prakṛtaṃ pravivicyate / yāvānsamasta evāyamadhvā prāṇe pratiṣṭhitaḥ dvidhā ca so@dhvā kriyayā mūrtyā ca pravibhajyate / prāṇa eva śikhā śrīmattriśirasyuditā hi sā baddhā yāgādikāle tuṃ niṣkalatvācchivātmikā / yato@horātramadhye@syāścaturviṃśatidhā gatiḥ prāṇavikṣeparandhrākhyaśataiścitraphalapradā / kṣapā śaśī tathāpāno nāda ekatra tiṣṭhati jīvādityo na codgacchettuṭyardhaṃ sāndhyamīdṛśam / ūrdhvavaktro raviścandro@dhomukho vahnirantare mādhyāhnikī mokṣadā syādvyomamadhyasthito raviḥ / anastamitasāro hi jantucakraprabodhakaḥ binduḥ prāṇo hyahaścaiva ravirekatra tiṣṭhati / mahāsandhyā tṛtīyā tu supraśāntātmikā sthitā evaṃ baddhā śikhā yatra tattatphalaniyojikā / ataḥ saṃvidi sarvo@yamadhvā viśramya tiṣṭhati amūrtāyāḥ sarvagatvānniṣkriyāyāśca saṃvidaḥ / mūrtikriyābhāsanaṃ yatsa evādhvā maheśituḥ adhvā krameṇa yātavye pade saṃprāptikāraṇam / dvaitināṃ bhogyabhāvāttu prabuddhānāṃ yato@dyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v31] Here one should examine words according to meaning everywhere, because it was said in auspicious night practice; the name here is considered threefold.

[tal-a06-v32] Occasional and well-known names, and another technical name; in priority one is principal, and then include therein.

[tal-a06-v33] Therefore this etymology of path is said; even if not stated, infer it by own intellect; how much is to be written in the book.

[tal-a06-v34] There the action-appearance path is called time; here three paths are clearly named letter, mantra, and word.

[tal-a06-v35] But the form-appearance part is declared the space-path; here three named kalaa, tattva, and pura are included.

[tal-a06-v36] In two triads here each has gross, subtle, and supreme body; therefore all this path is called sixfold.

[tal-a06-v37] The eastern triad of the sixfold path is again this same time-path, clearly established in breath.

[tal-a06-v38] This time, other than time in the middle, is called time; indeed it is the world-manifesting power of god.

[tal-a06-v39] The power of action is the supreme body of all principles; this lord principle is called Shiva's body.

[tal-a06-v40] This world-unity of experience is because this lord-formness is indeed in the supreme self.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-iha sarvatra śabdānāmanvarthaṃ carcayedyataḥ / uktaṃ śrīmanniśācāre saṃjñātra trividhā matā naimittikī prasiddhā ca tathānyā pāribhāṣikī / pūrvatve vā pradhānaṃ syāttatrāntarbhāvayettataḥ ato@dhvaśabdasyokteyaṃ niruktirnoditāpi cet / kvacitsvabuddhyā sāpyūhyā kiyallekhyaṃ hi pustake tatra kriyābhāsanaṃ yatso@dhvā kālāhva ucyate / varṇamantrapadābhikhyamatrāste@dhvatrayaṃ sphuṭam yastu mūrtyavabhāsāṃśaḥ sa deśādhvā nigadyate / kalātattvapurābhikhyamantarbhūtamiha trayam trikadvaye@tra pratyekaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ paraṃ vapuḥ / yato@sti tena sarvo@yamadhvā ṣaḍvidha ucyate ṣaḍvidhādadhvanaḥ prācyaṃ yadetattritayaṃ punaḥ / eṣa eva sa kālādhvā prāṇe spaṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ tattavamadhyasthitātkālādanyo@yaṃ kāla ucyate / eṣa kālo hi devasya viśvābhāsanakāriṇī kriyāśaktiḥ samastānāṃ tattvānāṃ ca paraṃ vapuḥ / etadīśvaratattvaṃ tacchivasya vapurucyate udriktābhogakāryātmaviśvaikātmyamidaṃ yataḥ / etadīśvararūpatvaṃ paramātmani yatkila

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v41] In that knower in maya, the time-principle is declared; it is Shiva's own body from shiva to pure knowledge.

[tal-a06-v42] That same becomes a sheath for the person from maya to attachment, because maya, arts, knowledge, and sada-shiva.

[tal-a06-v43] Lord, time, restriction, pure knowledge, and attachment are named; unattached are void-mother, intellect-mother, and sada-shiva.

[tal-a06-v44] Lord, breath-mother, knowledge, and body-knower-ness; unattached indeed is voidness, and knowledge indeed is intellect-ness.

[tal-a06-v45] World-self-ness and breath-ness are in the body; known-unity is by that, and world-measurement shines in the breath-path.

[tal-a06-v46] By which form we say that, let good ones consider it in this body, although everywhere.

[tal-a06-v47] Breath, though woven together, is not very clear; effort, life-only-self, and beyond that are considered twofold.

[tal-a06-v48] Knowable and unknowable are divided twofold; again by clear and unclear duality, each should be contemplated.

[tal-a06-v49] Prana, beautiful spanda of effort known as life, is not very clear from the kanda onward.

[tal-a06-v50] From the kanda support onward, the arrangement of channels is clearly said in Svacchanda as support of winds.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatpramātari māyīye kālatattvaṃ nigadyate / śivādiśuddhavidyāntaṃ yacchivasya svakaṃ vapuḥ tadeva puṃso māyādirāgāntaṃ kañcukībhavet / anāśritaṃ yato māyā kalāvidye sadāśivaḥ īśvaraḥ kālaniyatī sadvidyā rāga ucyate / anāśritaḥ śūnyamātā buddhimātā sadāśivaḥ īśvaraḥ prāṇamātā ca vidyā dehapramātṛtā / anāśrayo hi śūnyatvaṃ jñānameva hi buddhitā viśvātmatā ca prāṇatvaṃ dehe vedyaikatānatā / tena prāṇapathe viśvākalaneyaṃ virājate yena rūpeṇa tadvacmaḥ sadbhistadavadhīyatām / dvādaśāntāvadhāvasmindehe yadyapi sarvataḥ otaprotātmakaḥ prāṇastathāpītthaṃ na susphuṭaḥ / yatno jīvanamātrātmā tatparaśca dvidhā mataḥ saṃvedyaścāpyasaṃvedyo dvidhetthaṃ bhidyate punaḥ / sphuṭāsphuṭatvāddvaividhyaṃ pratyekaṃ paribhāvayet saṃvedyajīvanābhikhyaprayatnaspandasundaraḥ / prāṇaḥ kandātprabhṛtyeva tathāpyatra na susphuṭaḥ kandādhārātprabhṛtyeva vyavasthā tena kathyate / svacchandaśāstre nāḍīnāṃ vāyvādhāratayā sphuṭam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v51] There too that effort is not situated as knowable; but life-breath movement is distinguished from knowable effort from the heart.

[tal-a06-v52] Of lord Shiva, powers Vama, Jyeshtha, and Raudri are those two self-life-breaths causing effort.

[tal-a06-v53] Lord power is sometimes primary, as in limb wind stirring; self power sometimes, as in kanda contraction spanda.

[tal-a06-v54] Life power is sometimes in heart movement; clearly three or two may be primary for attentive yogis.

[tal-a06-v55] Even inversion toward primacy of life and self powers occurs from attention, unseen part, strength, and thus moving.

[tal-a06-v56] Vama is lord of bound beings and causing lord power; Jyeshtha is for well-awakened, and Raudri for those desiring to know.

[tal-a06-v57] Vama vomits samsara; Jyeshtha is Shiva-filled; Raudri melts diseases and obstructs all actions.

[tal-a06-v58] Not knowing the creation principle, one is not liberated nor liberates; in Shri Yogacara liberation is from all illumination.

[tal-a06-v59] Yogis who do not know creation, preservation, and dissolution are not liberated; they are bound by that ignorance.

[tal-a06-v60] Creation and related processes are all time-dependent, no doubt; that breath-essence is therefore clearly said as utterance.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatrāpi tu prayatno@sau na saṃvedyatayā sthitaḥ / vedyayatnāttu hṛdayātprāṇacāro vibhajyate prabhoḥ śivasya yā śaktirvāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrikā / satadanyatamāvātmaprāṇau yatnavidhāyinau prabhuśaktiḥ kvacinmukhyā yathāṅgamarudīraṇe / ātmaśaktiḥ kvacitkandasaṃkocaspandane yathā prāṇaśaktiḥ kvacitprāṇacāre hārde yathā sphuṭam / trayaṃ dvayaṃ vā mukhyaṃ syādyogināmavadhāninām avadhānādadṛṣṭāṃśādbalavattvādatheraṇāt / viparyayo@pi prāṇātmaśaktīnāṃ mukhyatāṃ prati vāmā saṃsāriṇāmīśā prabhuśaktirvidhāyinī / jyeṣṭhā tu suprabuddhānāṃ bubhutsūnāṃ ca raudrikā vāmā saṃsāravamanā jyeṣṭhā śivamayī yataḥ / drāvayitrī rujāṃ raudrī roddhrī cākhilakarmaṇām sṛṣṭyāditattvamajñātvā na mukto nāpi mocayet / uktaṃ ca śrīyogacāre mokṣaḥ sarvaprakāśanāt utpattisthitisaṃhārān ye na jānanti yoginaḥ / na muktāste tadajñānabandhanaikādhivāsitāḥ sṛṣṭyādayaśca te sarve kālādhīnā na saṃśayaḥ / sa ca prāṇātmakastasmāduccāraḥ kathyate sphuṭaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v61] Breath moves from the heart to the nose, thirty-six fingers long for every creature, measured by its own fingers.

[tal-a06-v62] In the smallest or largest body, such vigor, strength, pulsation, and breath movement are equal.

[tal-a06-v63] In the thirty-six-finger movement, the going-coming pair and the time totals are clearly situated.

[tal-a06-v64] The tuṭi has breaths joined with a quarter finger, sixteen exhaling and inhaling, and five parts per finger.

[tal-a06-v65] The tube of breath and exhalation is called day and night, with nine-finger ocean tuṭi and praharas.

[tal-a06-v66] At twilight of those two, the tuṭi measure applies, with ketu, sun, moon, and rahu.

[tal-a06-v67] Two praharas of others and planets' rising interval are named, with attainment, liberation, and black magic.

[tal-a06-v68] Worldly distance and nearness excellence are named; in eight praharas, midday and midnight give abhijit, liberation, and enjoyment.

[tal-a06-v69] Nakshatras and their others rise from the middle in order, with nagas, world-lord forms, ganeshas, and water principle.

[tal-a06-v70] Leaders extend up to pradhana, including vidya-principle leaders, sakala and others, up to throat and lip, and bhairavas.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-hṛdayātprāṇacāraśca nāsikyadvādaśāntataḥ / ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulo jantoḥ sarvasya svāṅgulakramāt kṣodiṣṭhe vā mahiṣṭhe vā dehe tādṛśa eva hi / vīryamojo balaṃ spandaḥ prāṇacāraḥ samaṃ tataḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule cāre yadgamāgamayugmakam / nālikātithimāsābdatatsaṅghro@tra sphuṭaṃ sthitaḥ tuṭiḥ sapādāṅgulayukprāṇastāḥ ṣoḍaśocchvasan / niḥśvasaṃścātra caṣakaḥ sapañcāṃśe@ṅgule@ṅgule śvāsapraśvāsayornālī proktāhorātra ucyate / navāṅgulāmbudhituṭau praharāste@bdhayo dinam nirgame@ntarniśenendū tayoḥ saṃdhye tuṭerdale / ketuḥ sūrye vidhau rāhurbhaumādervārabhāginaḥ praharadvayamanyeṣāṃ grahāṇāmudayo@ntarā / siddhirdavīyasī mokṣo@bhicāraḥ pāralaukikī aihikī dūranaikaṭyātiśayā praharāṣṭake / madhyāhnamadhyaniśayorabhijinmokṣabhogadā nakṣatrāṇāṃ tadanyeṣāmudayo madhyataḥ kramāt / nāgā lokeśamūrtīśā gaṇeśā jalatattvataḥ pradhānāntaṃ nāyakāśca vidyātattvādhināyakāḥ / sakalādyāśca kaṇṭhyoṣṭhyaparyantā bhairavāstathā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v71] Supreme powers, vama-sha, and hero leaders are named, eight and eight, enjoying pervaded-pervading state.

[tal-a06-v72] Gross and subtle things rise in order; in eight praharas of day and night, cruel and gentle actions occur without doubt.

[tal-a06-v73] Liberation, whether through cruelty or gentleness of intention, is determined at the destruction of day and night by pervasion, meditation, and yoga.

[tal-a06-v74] Those were also spoken by the supreme lord in the vira lineage: white and black, long and short, merit and demerit, in day and night.

[tal-a06-v75] If that initiation destroys day and night through pervasion, meditation, and yoga, then day and night are spoken in breath movement, and a month is called.

[tal-a06-v76] Day is dark, night is bright; fortnights act as before, and among the sixteen stated lunar days are those in east and west.

[tal-a06-v77] But in those, rest occurs half and half; the other fifteen lunar days, with a quarter and two fingers, divide day and night by a lunar day.

[tal-a06-v78] Indeed, those day and night depend on light and rest, so awareness occurs every moment, because the yogini is light and bliss.

[tal-a06-v79] Those two are fixed: as much as by that, so much day and night, because awareness is clearly risen and set.

[tal-a06-v80] A moment, eon, or blink is only that much; let it be so, as much as the rising of awareness devoted to grasping one object.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śaktayaḥ pārameśvaryo vāmaśā vīranāyakāḥ / aṣṭāvaṣṭau ye ya itthaṃ vyāpyavyāpakatājuṣaḥ sthūlasūkṣmāḥ kramātteṣāmudayaḥ praharāṣṭake / dine krūrāṇi saumyāni rātrau karmāṇyasaṃśayam krūratā saumyatā vābhisandherapi nirūpitā / dinarātrikṣaye muktiḥ sā vyāptidhyānayogataḥ te coktāḥ parameśena śrīmadvīrāvalīkule / sitāsitau dīrghahrasvau dharmādharmau dinakṣape kṣīyete yadi taddīkṣā vyāptyā dhyānena yogataḥ / ahorātraḥ prāṇacāre kathito māsa ucyate dinaṃ kṛṣṇo niśā śuklaḥ pakṣau karmasu pūrvavat / yāḥ ṣoḍaśoktāstithayastāsu ye pūrvapaścime tayostu viśramo@rdhe@rdhe tithyaḥ pañcadaśetarāḥ / sapāde dvyaṅgule tithyā ahorātro vibhajyate prakāśaviśramavaśāttāveva hi dinakṣape / saṃvitpratikṣaṇaṃ yasmātprakāśānandayoginī tau klṛptau yāvati tayā tāvatyeva dinakṣape / yāvatyeva hi saṃvittiruditoditasusphuṭā tāvāneva kṣaṇaḥ kalpo nimeṣo vā tadastvapi / yāvānevodayo vittervedyaikagrahatatparaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v81] Setting is only that much: the knower's self-chewing occurs in the object, outside or inside, in two, or in the abandonment of two.

[tal-a06-v82] In every way, becoming that is day; knower abiding is night; the known rests, and the knower is an inward-facing state.

[tal-a06-v83] Formerly, after examining being-only-form, waking knower-ness is dream, and the knower state is ancient.

[tal-a06-v84] Supreme sleep, in the destruction of night and day, is the fourth nondual; sometimes chewing occurs through object-rest sameness in the self.

[tal-a06-v85] That equality of known and knower is the equality of night and day; rest is greater in the known for the length of day.

[tal-a06-v86] Self-rest may be deficient in the opposite; reversal occurs, for when one is awakened in eagerness for self, rest in the known is small.

[tal-a06-v87] Thus one would state the order of day-night deficiency and excess, as in bodies day and night are not equal.

[tal-a06-v88] So too in cities it is declared by that distinction, by the sun of Shri Traiyambaka.

[tal-a06-v89] Shri Shambhu thus spread the day-night order to me; Shri Santanaguru said the place of awakened and unawakened.

[tal-a06-v90] Beginning from the heart, the night-day division by that is within the false white side, the part of entering delight.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tāvadevāstamayanaṃ veditṛsvātmacarvaṇam / vedye ca bahirantarvā dvaye vātha dvayojjhite sarvathā tanmayībhūtirdinaṃ vettṛsthatā niśā / veditā vedyaviśrānto vettā tvantarmukhasthitiḥ purā vicārayanpaścātsattāmātrasvarūpakaḥ / jāgradveditṛtā svapno vettṛbhāvaḥ purātanaḥ paraḥ suptaṃ kṣaye rātridinayosturyamadvayam / kadācidvastuviśrāntisāmyenātmani carvaṇam vedyavedakasāmyaṃ tat sā rātridinatulyatā / vedye viśrāntiradhikā dinadairghyāya tatra tu nyūnā syātsvātmaviśrāntirviparīte viparyayaḥ / svātmautsukye prabuddhe hi vedyaviśrāntiralpikā itthameva divārātrinyūnādhikyakramaṃ vadet / yathā deheṣvahorātranyūnādhikyādi no samam tathā pureṣvapītyevaṃ tadviśeṣeṇa noditam / śrītraiyambakasantānavitatāmbarabhāskaraḥ dinarātrikramaṃ me śrīśaṃbhuritthamapaprathat / śrīsantānagurustvāha sthānaṃ buddhāprabuddhayoḥ hṛda ārabhya yattena rātrindivavibhājanam / tadasatsitapakṣe@ntaḥ praveśollāsabhāgini

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v100] There on pratipada, that prior half of the half-tuti being new-moon, by lunar-day-cut one performs and enters the solar eclipse.

[tal-a06-v91] How can the unawakened place be day? Enough with this; this is not my prior opinion.

[tal-a06-v92] But shown to disciples, seers of the true path explain the dark fortnight, the moon gone to breath.

[tal-a06-v93] By nourishing the self one by one, one digit is abandoned each tithi; near the twelve-end, that fifteenth drop remains.

[tal-a06-v94] Here at new moon the waned moon enters the breath-sun; it is said in Shri Kamika, and supreme nature, Maya, proceeds in half-halves in two-part Shiva form.

[tal-a06-v95] By moon-sun self the body is filled and dissolved; nectar is by moon form, twofold and sixteenfold again.

[tal-a06-v96] All gods drink the ten-five supreme digits; new moon remains in the cave and nourishes the world.

[tal-a06-v97] Thus the fifteen digits of the moon are consumed in order; the sixteenth, identical with nourishing immortal form, is not consumed.

[tal-a06-v98] There the fifteen-digit portion is the tuṭi of the waned moon; its upper half is called the fortnight-juncture.

[tal-a06-v99] Therefore from rest in the half-tuti at new moon, the prior half, the supreme pratipada, and the other half — that juncture is posited.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-abuddhasthānamevaitaddinatvena kathaṃ bhavet / alaṃ vānena nedaṃ vā mama prāṅmatamatsaraḥ heye tu darśite śiṣyāḥ satpathaikāntadarśinaḥ / vyākhyātaḥ kṛṣṇapakṣo ya statra prāṇagataḥ śaśī āpyāyanātmanaikaikāṃ kalāṃ pratitithi tyajet / dvādaśāntasamīpe tu yāsau pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ sāmāvasyātra sa kṣīṇaścandraḥ prāṇārkamāviśet / uktaṃ śrīkāmikāyāṃ ca nordhve@dhaḥ prakṛtiḥ parā / ardhārdhe kramate māyā dvikhaṇḍā śivarūpiṇī candrasūryātmanā dehaṃ pūrayetpravilāpayet / amṛtaṃ candrarūpeṇa dvidhā ṣoḍaśadhā punaḥ pivanti ca surāḥ sarve daśapañca parāḥ kalāḥ / amā śeṣaguhāntaḥsthāmāvāsyā viśvatarpiṇī evaṃ kalāḥ pañcadaśa kṣīyante śaśinaḥ kramāt / āpyāyinyamṛtābrūpatādātmyātṣoḍaśī na tu tatra pañcadaśī yāsau tuṭiḥ prakṣīṇacandramāḥ / tadūrdhvagaṃ yattuṭyardhaṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ sa kīrtitaḥ tasmādviśramatuṭyardhādāmāvasyaṃ purādalam / paraṃ prātipadaṃ cārdhamiti saṃdhiḥ sa kalpyate tatra prātipade tasmiṃstuṭyardhārdhe purādalam / āmāvasyaṃ tithicchedātkuryātsūryagrahaṃ viśat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v101] There in the solar disc the moon, dissolved, drips its honey; once heated, the sun-companion — Simhika's son — drinks that honey.

[tal-a06-v102] The sun is the measure, the moon the measurable, both knowledge-and-action-natured; Rahu the maya-observer is skilled at covering them.

[tal-a06-v103] From that clash, the darkness-natured one cannot melt them; from the union of the two, the primary measurer is the melter.

[tal-a06-v104] From the clash of sun, moon and Rahu: measure, knowable and knower as non-dual — therefore this great graha is meritorious.

[tal-a06-v105] Even without new-moon this clash is a great graha — as when the sun is in Aries and Rahu in Asvini on an Asvini day.

[tal-a06-v106] When on new-moon the half is dissolved in the half of pratipada and the pratipadi is fully pure — that is liberation in the distant rite.

[tal-a06-v107] Between eclipse and liberation: bathing, meditation, homa, japa and the rest — worldly and unworldly — their further fruit becomes beyond-worldly.

[tal-a06-v108] Entering the moment of dissolution of the eclipsed and eclipsor disturbance, one performs liberation-share meditation, worship and the rest at the moon-sun eclipse.

[tal-a06-v109] Lunar-day cut brings debt, cough, increase, exhalation, wealth; effortless and effort-born signs differ by exhalation and restraint.

[tal-a06-v110] Thus breath enters the consciousness-sun, which fills the nectar-filled moon one by one with consciousness-rays by measure.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatrārkamaṇḍale līnaḥ śaśī sravati yanmadhu / taptatvāttatpibedindusahabhūḥ siṃhikāsutaḥ arkaḥ pramāṇaṃ somastu meyaṃ jñānakriyātmakau / rāhurmāyāpramātā syāttadācchādanakovidaḥ tata eva tamorūpo vilāpayitumakṣamaḥ / tatsaṃghaṭṭādvayollāso mukhyo mātā vilāpakaḥ arkendurāhusaṃghaṭṭāt pramāṇaṃ vedyavedakau / advayena tatastena puṇya eṣa mahāgrahaḥ amāvasyāṃ vināpyeṣa saṃghaṭṭaścenmahāgrahaḥ / yathārke meṣage rāhāvaśvinīsthe@śvinīdine āmāvāsyaṃ yadā tvardhaṃ līnaṃ prātipade dale / pratipacca viśuddhā syāttanmokṣo dūrage vidhau grāsamokṣāntare snānadhyānahomajapādikam / laukikālaukikaṃ bhūyaḥphalaṃ syātpāralaukikam grāsyagrāsakatākṣobhaprakṣaye kṣaṇamāviśan / mokṣabhāgdhyānapūjādi kurvaṃścandrārkayorgrahe tithiccheda ṛṇaṃ kāso vṛddhirniḥśvasanaṃ dhanam / ayatnajaṃ yatnajaṃ tu recanādatha rodhanāt evaṃ prāṇe viśati citsūrya induṃ sudhāmayam / ekaikadhyena bodhāṃśu kalayā paripūrayet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v111] These fifteen lunar days of the bright fortnight are beautiful moon-nectar days.

[tal-a06-v112] At the last full lunar day there is previous fortnight junction; moon seizure occurs at first-day junction from previous entry.

[tal-a06-v113] Here worldly seizure gives practitioners great fruit; another month is called breath-course.

[tal-a06-v114] Sun standing in six fingers from heart through capricorn makes the sixfold northern course.

[tal-a06-v115] After three transits and eighteen fingers, when sun reaches aries, there is meritorious otherworldly equinox.

[tal-a06-v116] When sun enters libra, that same becomes equinox here, giving success in southern course.

[tal-a06-v117] Embryo state, desire to manifest, manifesting, future becoming, and beginning of manifestation are described.

[tal-a06-v118] Birth, being, change, growth, decline, and decay occur in order from capricorn; action here produces similar fruit.

[tal-a06-v119] In otherworldly context, fish and pitcher from mantra etc prior service yield fourfold increasing result.

[tal-a06-v120] Indeed entry there itself yields beautiful worldly action of peace and nourishment, with fruit increasingly distant in order.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kramasaṃpūraṇāśāliśaśāṅkāmṛtasundarāḥ / tuṭyaḥ pañcadaśaitāḥ syustithayaḥ sitapakṣagāḥ antyāyāṃ pūrṇamastuṭyāṃ pūrvavatpakṣasandhitā / indugrahaśca pratipatsandhau pūrvapraveśataḥ aihikaṃ grahaṇe cātra sādhakānāṃ mahāphalam / prāgvadanyadayaṃ māsaḥ prāṇacāre@bda ucyate ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsvaṅguleṣvarko hṛdayānmakarādiṣu / tiṣṭhanmāghāḍhikaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ kuryāttaccottarāyaṇam saṃkrāntitritaye vṛtte bhukte cāṣṭādaśāṅgule / meṣaṃ prāpte ravau puṇyaṃ viṣuvatpāralaukikam praveśe tu tulāsthe@rke tadeva viṣuvadbhavet / iha siddhipradaṃ caitaddakṣiṇāyanagaṃ tataḥ garbhatā prodbubhūṣiṣyadbhāvaścāthodbubhūṣutā / udbhaviṣyattvamudbhūtiprārambho@pyudbhavasthitiḥ janma sattā pariṇatirvṛddhirhrāsaḥ kṣayaḥ kramāt / makarādīni tenātra kriyā sūte sadṛkphalam āmutrike jhaṣaḥ kumbho mantrādeḥ pūrvasevane / catuṣkaṃ kila mīnādyamantikaṃ cottarottaram praveśe khalu tatraiva śāntipuṣṭyādisundaram / karma syādaihikaṃ tacca dūradūraphalaṃ kramāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v121] At the outgoing day increases; reversed, it counter-changes — in this year five tithis run per finger-width, such is the order.

[tal-a06-v122] There too the day-night ordinance stands as before; in the breath-year the months from Kārtika on are measured deftly.

[tal-a06-v123] Up to the Great-Father the Rudras would be, future, here at the first of twelve; in breath the year-rise is declared — now the twelve-year rise.

[tal-a06-v124] The dark-fortnight tithis, in each single finger-width in order, within the twelve-year rise — twelve arisen, beginning with Caitra.

[tal-a06-v125] In Caitra a mantra-rise appears; joined to the palate and again at the heart, thereby the Caitra-rise stands — the mantra-rise too.

[tal-a06-v126] Per finger-width the tithis are posited in three hundred; in the five-part finger-width the year would be, in breath, by sixty-year measure again.

[tal-a06-v127] Six hundreds and twenty-one thousands — this division, arising in breath, is called the sixty-year day and night.

[tal-a06-v128] Whatever division and juncture stands there among prahara, half-day, night, month, season, year and sun — that juncture is sacred for meditation and worship.

[tal-a06-v129] Thus in the breath-rise this time — single-bodied as power, world-self dwelling within — has its outer form posed.

[tal-a06-v130] Six breaths make a cup, sixty a tube; there the tithi by thirty makes the month, and twelve of those make the year.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nirgame dinavṛddhiḥ syādviparīte viparyayaḥ / varṣe@smiṃstithayaḥ pañca pratyaṅgulamiti kramaḥ tatrāpyahorātravidhiriti sarvaṃ hi pūrvavat / prāṇīye varṣa etasminkārtikādiṣu dakṣataḥ pitāmahāntaṃ rudrāḥ syurdvādaśāgre@tra bhāvinaḥ / prāṇe varṣodayaḥ prokto dvādaśābdodayo@dhunā kharasāstithya ekasminnekasminnaṅgule kramāt / dvādaśābdodaye te ca caitrādyā dvādaśoditāḥ caitre mantroditiḥ so@pi tālunyukto@dhunā punaḥ / hṛdi caitroditistena tatra mantrodayo@pi hi pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ tu triśate parikalpite / sapañcāṃśāṅgule@bdaḥ syātprāṇe ṣaṣṭyabdatā punaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi caikaviṃśatirityayam / vibhāgaḥ prāṇagaḥ ṣaṣṭivarṣāhorātra ucyate praharāharniśāmāsaṛtvabdaraviṣaṣṭigaḥ / yaśchedastatra yaḥ sandhiḥ sa puṇyo dhyānapūjane iti prāṇodaye yo@yaṃ kālaḥ śaktyekavigrahaḥ / viśvātmāntaḥsthitastasya bāhye rūpaṃ nirūpyate ṣaṭ prāṇāścaṣakasteṣāṃ ṣaṣṭirnālī ca tāstathā / tithistattriṃśatā māsaste dvādaśa tu vatsaraḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v131] The year of the Fathers is a day and night, from the north-south course; by their own measure that year is called divine.

[tal-a06-v132] Three hundred sixty years here are human; that, divided by twelve, yields the month-number here.

[tal-a06-v133] Having destroyed that day-night reckoning by thirty, one should say it; having destroyed it again by twenty-one thousand and six hundred, one should say it.

[tal-a06-v134] There one should state the breath-count, with its sixty-year beginning; again it was said by teachers in their own commentaries beginning with the glorious Raurava.

[tal-a06-v135] The day-night of the gods is a year for humans; by three hundred and sixty, the year of men becomes a god-year.

[tal-a06-v136] And in the glorious Svachanda scripture that very opinion is seen: beginning with that day-night of the ancestors, and afterwards.

[tal-a06-v137] Thus the divine day-night is indeed concluded in unity; by that, the teachers who derive it from the two statements of the glorious Svachanda.

[tal-a06-v138] They deludedly called the ancestral year a divine day, in vain; thousands of divine sun-years occur in the ages, from four onward.

[tal-a06-v139] By one each decrease, among those hundreds there are eight junctions; fourteen Manus span seventy-one four-ages.

[tal-a06-v140] There in Brahma's hand fourteen Indras proceed in order; at the end of Brahma's day, the flame of time-fire measures a lakh yojanas.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-abdaṃ pitryastvahorātra udagdakṣiṇato@yanāt / pitṝṇāṃ yatsvamānena varṣaṃ taddivyamucyate ṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ ca triśataṃ varṣāṇāmatra mānuṣam / tacca dvādaśabhirhatvā māsasaṃkhyātra labhyate tāṃ punastriṃśatā hatvāhorātrakalpanā vadet / hatvā tāṃ caikaviṃśatyā sahasraiḥ ṣaṭśatena ca prāṇasaṃkhyāṃ vadettatra ṣaṣṭyādyabdodayaṃ punaḥ / uktaṃ ca gurubhiḥ śrīmadrauravādisvavṛttiṣu devānāṃ yadahorātraṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ sa hāyanaḥ / śatatrayeṇa ṣaṣṭyā ca nṝṇāṃ vibudhavatsaraḥ śrīmatsvacchandaśāstre ca tadeva matamīkṣyate / pitṝṇāṃ tadahorātramityupakramya pṛṣṭhataḥ evaṃ daivastvahorātra iti hyaikyopasaṃhṛtiḥ / tena ye guravaḥ śrīmatsvacchandoktidvayāditaḥ pitryaṃ varṣaṃ divyadinamūcurbhrāntā hi te mudhā / divyārkābdasahasrāṇi yugeṣu caturāditaḥ ekaikahānyā tāvadbhiḥ śataisteṣvaṣṭa saṃdhayaḥ / caturyugaikasaptatyā manvantaste caturdaśa brahmaṇo@hastatra cendrāḥ kramādyānti caturdaśa / brahmāho@nte kālavahnerjvālā yojanalakṣiṇī

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v141] Having burned the three worlds, by smoke it puts another three to sleep, before the hells, since the manifestation of time-fire.

[tal-a06-v142] "The Lord is stationed below, O Ishvara"—thus is the glorious Raurava opinion: when Brahma's breath is blown away, in ashes, by sweat water.

[tal-a06-v143] The universe flooded by that remains until the arrival of night; at the end of that night, all beings have subtle bodies.

[tal-a06-v144] Impelled by fire-speed, people in the world become dissolution only; while Kushmanda, Hataka, and others play in the great abode.

[tal-a06-v145] At night's end he makes creation again, begun from darkness; at the end of his own hundred years stands that ruin — the Vaiṣṇava day.

[tal-a06-v146] And the night is of that measure — thus the hundreds named Viṣṇu and Rudra, in order at each one's own hundred-end, perish here with the egg's waning.

[tal-a06-v147] Thus at the ends of the unmanifest tattva from the start, a hundred years in order — the day-night division would so obtain, measured by each one's own hundred-year span.

[tal-a06-v148] By thousands of Brahmā's dissolution-joys with the rasāgni fires — among the Rudras standing in the unmanifest, day and night are each of that measure.

[tal-a06-v149] Then Śrīkaṇṭha alone would be the lord directly doing dissolution; all the Rudras likewise at the root are charged with māyā's womb.

[tal-a06-v150] In the one named avyakta he indeed sits with Śrīkaṇṭha of Brahmā's line, lower work withdrawn — for Brahmā is there in the lower reach of thought.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-dagdhvā lokatrayaṃ dhūmāttvanyatprasvāpayettrayam / nirayebhyaḥ purā kālavahnervyaktiryatastataḥ vibhuradhaḥsthito@pīśa iti śrīrauravaṃ matam / brahmaniḥśvāsanirdhūte bhasmani svedavāriṇā tadīyenāplutaṃ viśvaṃ tiṣṭhettāvanniśāgame / tasminniśāvadhau sarve pudgalāḥ sūkṣmadehagāḥ agnivegeritā loke jane syurlayakevalāḥ / kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakādyāstu krīḍanti mahadālaye niśākṣaye punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ kurute tāmasāditaḥ / svakavarṣaśatānte@sya kṣayastadvaiṣṇavaṃ dinam rātriśca tāvatītyevaṃ viṣṇurudraśatābhidhāḥ / kramātsvasvaśatānteṣu naśyantyatrāṇḍalopataḥ abādyavyaktatattvānteṣvitthaṃ varṣaśataṃ kramāt / dinarātrivibhāgaḥ syāt svasvāyuḥśatamānataḥ brahmaṇaḥ pralayollāsasahasraistu rasāgnibhiḥ / avyaktastheṣu rudreṣu dinaṃ rātriśca tāvatī tadā śrīkaṇṭha eva syātsākṣātsaṃhārakṛtprabhuḥ / sarve rudrāstathā mūle māyāgarbhādhikāriṇaḥ avyaktākhye hyāviriñcācchrīkaṇṭhena sahāsate / nivṛttādhaḥsthakarmā hi brahmā tatrādhare dhiyaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v151] The knower in office is not the mere experiencer; having turned only to Śiva he would become Śiva — this intermediate laya at its end is called creation.

[tal-a06-v152] At that day's face Śrīkaṇṭha creates again toward those perfected in Sāṃkhya, Vedas, and the rest — yet complete liberation is not of this kind.

[tal-a06-v153] In pradhāna the day-night born of it — a hundred years of the Lord — is Śrīkaṇṭha's lifespan, the day of those dwelling in the kañcukas.

[tal-a06-v154] From that sequence Niyati, Kāla, Rāga, Vidyā, and Kalā enter one another's dissolution; their lifespan is the dense day.

[tal-a06-v155] At that day's wasting the universe dissolves in māyā; in the night of that measure Gahaneśa should create again.

[tal-a06-v156] Thus the unmanifest time is struck through by ten parārdhas; māyā's night of that measure would be the dissolution — that is the one so named.

[tal-a06-v157] The maya-time, multiplied by half-counts and by a hundred, becomes the lordly day; sound and breath create the world.

[tal-a06-v158] During that lordly night, breath subsides, and the universe, contained in the breath-womb, moves by the sushumna path.

[tal-a06-v159] When breath is pacified in the brahma cavity, consciousness also remains; dissolution of this proceeds part by part, from subtle to subtler.

[tal-a06-v160] Multiplying the lordly time by half-counts and by a hundred gives the sadashiva day; the night is the great dissolution.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na bhoktā jño@dhikāre tu vṛtta eva śivībhavet / sa eṣo@vāntaralayastatkṣaye sṛṣṭirucyate sāṃkhyavedādisaṃsiddhāñchrīkaṇṭhastadaharmukhe / sṛjatyeva punastena na samyaṅmuktirīdṛśī pradhāne yadahorātraṃ tajjaṃ varṣaśataṃ vibhoḥ / śrīkaṇṭhasyāyuretacca dinaṃ kañcukavāsinām tatkramānniyatiḥ kālo rāgo vidyā kaletyamī / yāntyanyonyaṃ layaṃ teṣāmāyurgāhanikaṃ dinam taddinaprakṣaye viśvaṃ māyāyāṃ pravilīyate / kṣīṇāyāṃ niśi tāvatyāṃ gahaneśaḥ sṛjetpunaḥ evamavyaktakālaṃ tu parārdhairdaśabhirjahi / māyāhastāvatī rātrirbhavetpralaya eṣa saḥ māyākālaṃ parārdhānāṃ guṇayitvā śatena tu / aiśvaro divaso nādaḥ prāṇātmātra sṛjejjagat tāvatī caiśvarī rātriryatra prāṇaḥ praśāmyati / prāṇagarbhasthamapyatra viśvaṃ sauṣumnavartmanā prāṇe brahmavile śānte saṃvidyāpyavaśiṣyate / aṃśāṃśikāto@pyetasyāḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmataro layaḥ guṇayitvaiśvaraṃ kālaṃ parārdhānāṃ śatena tu / sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ rātrirmahāpralaya eva ca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v161] At the end of his time, sadashiva occupies the bindu, crescent, and obstructing powers, takes the moving and still universe, and dissolves into sound.

[tal-a06-v162] Sound, by its end-operation, pierces the brahma cavity and suddenly goes to dissolution in the shakti principle at the end of its own time.

[tal-a06-v163] Thus far is to be known: shakti dissolves again into the pervading principle at the end of its own time, day and night.

[tal-a06-v164] The pervading principle dissolves that day and night; it remains unsupported, even when shakti time is struck and unsupported.

[tal-a06-v165] At that time, day and night occur; even time multiplied by half-counts goes to dissolution in the state named equality, the samanasa state.

[tal-a06-v166] That time, named equality, would be eternal and auspicious, made of parts; its samanasa form is equality, brahman, all-pervading.

[tal-a06-v167] Therefore, from samanasa time, from the measure of a blink onward, minute and so forth up to the end of half-counts is produced; this is established here.

[tal-a06-v168] The series runs: ten hundred thousand ten thousand, laksha, niyuta, koti, with arbuda, vṛnda, kharva, nikharva, shankha, lotus, ocean, middle, end, and then half-count.

[tal-a06-v169] From one onward, counting tenfold by order, one should declare the state among eighteen.

[tal-a06-v170] These four are principal dissolutions and creations, their moments, and the four egg-worlds.

[tal-a06-v171] Time-fire destroys on earth; at maya's end the time-principle king, Shrikantha, root, makes creation and destruction in one place.

[tal-a06-v172] From that intermediate dissolution, glorious Aghora, lord of creation and dissolution, destroys and creates at power's end.

[tal-a06-v173] In its creation, countless creation-destructions of worlds are included; therefore shakti is called the great creation.

[tal-a06-v174] In dissolution, Brahma, Hari, and Rudras proceed mutually by order to dissolution at maya's end.

[tal-a06-v175] In maya-principle dissolution these go to the supreme state; above maya, white-path dwellers dissolve in supreme Shiva.

[tal-a06-v176] There too, by conditional difference in dissolution, knowers know difference; thus in the truth-lord group, dissolved, creation returns to the supreme.

[tal-a06-v177] Its practitioners, desired by Shiva, dwell in its place; Brahmi, power of the supreme, should be cast there.

[tal-a06-v178] Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra and others follow order from Vaishnavi etc; leaving another power-holder, power does not go to such.

[tal-a06-v179] Covered and manifested all; power and Shiva are one; thus creations and dissolutions are established in one place.

[tal-a06-v180] He too is in consciousness; pure consciousness, devoid of knowable, is only pure consciousness; the goddess is the supreme lady.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v181] The thirty-eighth principle is the heart, supreme and inferior, by which consciousness itself pulsates by nature.

[tal-a06-v182] Thus dissolution and arising are praised in breath through the sixty-year cycle, established by will alone, with discussion of action's variety.

[tal-a06-v183] Time power arises from that; the external body is not fixed, whether in dream, sleep, or thought's range.

[tal-a06-v184] In samadhi, distinguishing universe dissolution and creation, even a measured portion of time shines extensively.

[tal-a06-v185] In difference of knowers, variegated extensiveness appears; thus in breath time is born from the power of action variety.

[tal-a06-v186] So in apana too, spreading from the heart's root seat, contraction and expansion of the great root seat occur.

[tal-a06-v187] For brahma and supported ends, creation and dissolution are gathered; although apana always carries thus, that is different.

[tal-a06-v188] Unperceived effort is worshipped by yogis through effort, reaching the end of twelve heart-bulb bliss contractions and expansions.

[tal-a06-v189] Brahma and unsupported ends are served here by good yogis, and these dwell in the universe by supreme lord power.

[tal-a06-v190] Thus obtaining the body, its causes are stated in Kamika through childhood, youth, old age, death, and rebirth.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v191] In liberation and body, brahma and others act in six seats; at the end the supreme goddess is where the joined one is not born.

[tal-a06-v192] By this alone, when known, one becomes the doer of initiation and grace, because all causes unfold in the well-known state.

[tal-a06-v193] One who finds causeless Shiva, the cause of the universe, sees this downward-facing form that utterly destroys the stain of duality.

[tal-a06-v194] In that worship, the upper and lower drumming ceases; there, at the rise of apana, join sixty-year cycles as before.

[tal-a06-v195] As long as one performs with tuṭi and so on according to finger divisions, the rule is the same even in the heart nadis.

[tal-a06-v196] Moving in all directions, it is conceived tenfold; ten principal great nadis fill those gone there.

[tal-a06-v197] A nadi residing in another nadi has all positions in the body; moving in eight directions, this moves according to the direction-lord's order.

[tal-a06-v198] Imitating actions, fierce and gentle, he shines; indeed in three nadis, left, right, and middle.

[tal-a06-v199] Moving and staying day and night in the principal moon, sun, and fire channels, two and a half nalikas, nine hundred pranas are established.

[tal-a06-v200] Flowing so much day and night, he moves in twenty-four ways; on the equinox day, in the morning, with fractions, a nali, he is middle-going.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v201] Left and other north-right until five transits; thus when the nalis are diminished to fourteen minus a quarter.

[tal-a06-v202] At midday, the right equinox flow of nine hundred pranas flows; right, north, other, north, right, again five transits.

[tal-a06-v205] Beginning with day and night increase and decrease, transit goes; night end and day first parts, midday, day decay.

[tal-a06-v206] That night rise, middle spoken, pervasion seen; in pervasion pervading going function, equality and pervasion is called.

[tal-a06-v207] That deserves, and which time equinox spoken there; from equinox decrease and increase, which day night going.

[tal-a06-v208] By that order only transit decrease increase of day night; thus equal wind two year alternation.

[tal-a06-v209] Motion in one place, not here breath practice; even equal tuṭi before up to sixty year range.

[tal-a06-v210] Time number very subtle single motion going is counted by wise; dawn morning midday midnight etc which indeed.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v211] Inner transit going to be grasped, that chief from that fruit rise; spoken equal going time in udana but is determined.

[tal-a06-v221] At entry the letters stand at the twelve-end, forehead, throat, and heart, with bindu and visarga stationed around them.

[tal-a06-v222] Within the first letter of the ka-five, ever-arising, that same letter-continuity runs inside the six-placed letters.

[tal-a06-v223] In the heart the s-letter is life in breath-form, the bindu light, and the hārṇa stands as fullness itself.

[tal-a06-v224] This highest arising of letters is called subtle: at entry, sixteen-facing, the solar ones stand apart from the ṣaṇṭhā.

[tal-a06-v225] These letters are the moon-sun measures; this subtle arising is half-measure time — thirty-three of the ka-series, it is called.

[tal-a06-v226] Shorts are five, longs eight, with twice, thrice, pluta, and lṝ: our guru calls these eighty-one half-measures.

[tal-a06-v227] By whose will the Lord uttered the eighty-one-letter mantra: the Goddess of eighty-one words is the power, told of as Śiva's own.

[tal-a06-v228] In the glorious Mātaṅga, whose self is the dharma-mass, is Śiva, from whom it comes — the parāmarśa wheel's lord, the ruler.

[tal-a06-v229] The coarse recitation of eighty-one words is manifested through reflection, and from that the reflection is completed as one.

[tal-a06-v230] So long that word is spoken, not bound by sleep-verb rule, but empowered by the great reflection of eighty-one words.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v231] The coarse means is indeed this supreme means, a dissolution made by measure, with half-measures nine and nine in four and four.

[tal-a06-v232] Thus in the fingers thirty-six and eighty-one words arise; when a finger is divided by a ninth part, ninth portions result.

[tal-a06-v233] The Vedas, another half-measure, twice-four-six multiplied, three; thus light goes through two sets of four finger-hole portions.

[tal-a06-v234] Long, prolated, gradually two-three multiplied half; from that also consonant, ksha is three half-measures, measured, with intervals between.

[tal-a06-v235] When its resting half-measure is counted, in that finger half by a third part, then half-measure occurs before and again.

[tal-a06-v236] Ksha is the self of all combination-grasping, but all-pervading, ruler and share of all letter arising from beginning to end and junctions.

[tal-a06-v237] Thus in the thirty-six course letters arise; in cruel or gentle result, in reverse from ha until the last.

[tal-a06-v238] Heart-a at the twelfth end, ha-letter; knowers know this as i-self nondual, which is rest in the self of light.

[tal-a06-v239] By nondivision of Shiva and Shakti, this eighty-one measure circulates in seventy-two fingers by doubling.

[tal-a06-v240] Subtle arising is threefold, supreme arising is twofold; now coarse arising of letters is spoken by the teacher.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a06-v241] Some say eight vargas rise by half a watch each day, with decrease and increase at night, while others disagree.

[tal-a06-v242] This varga rise, moving by half a watch day and night, is counted as thirteen hundred fifty breaths.

[tal-a06-v243] Indeed, one and a half transitions occur per varga in day and night, and four hundred twenty-seven rise.

[tal-a06-v244] For the nine vargas, one hundred breaths are assigned, and a one-third transition per varga is stated.

[tal-a06-v245] In the union of day and night, the gross varga rise, counted in hundreds, is called by this ocean-like name.

[tal-a06-v246] Each letter has two hundred sixteen breaths, thus also at night and outside.

[tal-a06-v247] There, one hundred eight raudra and shakta are counted, and rudra and shakti remain indivisible in yamala union.

[tal-a06-v248] In day-night division, sight, fire, water, moon, and recitation with a fifth part nadi are remembered as outside letter rise.

[tal-a06-v249] Thus this fifty-verse discussion of letters is completed; some call it one less, and we declare their opinion.

[tal-a06-v250] Four vedas, fifth part less, and one each of four halves are more in a letter, doubled and indivisible in day and night.
